text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P1 — GPU pool "west-eu-gpu" capacity below 20% (available gpus=6/32). Queue growth detected: 1,200 pending requests. Avg queue length +75% in last 5m. Autoscaler attempts: 3 failed. Pager sent to @priya_oncall and @olivia_oncall.

priya_oncall: ack — I'm on it. Looking at autoscaler and driver metrics now. Can someone post the most recent driver logs?

dan_engineer: grabbing logs from nodes 18-22. seeing repeated CUDA/Xid errors + OOMs. gist incoming.

dan_engineer: ```
Mar 15 11:02:18 node-18 kernel: NVRM: Xid (ECC): 79, PID 1342, GPU 0
Mar 15 11:02:19 node-19 containerd: runtime: oom killed process model_server
Mar 15 11:03:05 node-20 nvidia: driver_init: failed to create context: out of memory
Mar 15 11:03:05 node-20 systemd: kubelet: node lost GPU capability
``` 

lee_infra: autoscaler requests show nodes provisioning but kubelet reports "gpu-driver-not-ready" and kube-scheduler refuses pods due to taint `gpu.unavailable:NoSchedule`.

olivia_oncall: any signs of noisy tenants or one workload hogging everything? we should identify top token consumers.

infra-bot: top 5 jobs by GPU token/sec: job-9923 (48%), job-9911 (22%), job-3010 (9%), job-7000 (6%), job-1001 (4%).

priya_oncall: ok noisy tenant job-9923 is ~half the load. can we throttle its concurrency or move it to a different pool? @sara_pager can ops contact customer? @coco_support FYI for customer-impact comms.

sara_pager: pinged product-contact for job-9923. Trying to flip to lower-parity model (faster cheaper) for 9923 — they allowed fallback in SLA.

lee_infra: attempted manual scale +4 nodes via infra CLI but nodes booted and then immediately reported driver crash loop. kube shows `container runtime: failed prestart`.

priya_oncall: so autoscaler failing + manual nodes failing -> effective capacity stuck ~6 gpus. Need immediate mitigation: 1) divert traffic to us-east-gpu pool, 2) enable model fallback for noisy tenant, 3) enforce per-tenant rate-limits. Who can run the routing switch?

dan_engineer: I can flip a route for non-SLA tenants to us-east. Running: `redwood route update --pool west-eu-gpu --fallback us-east-gpu --filter tenant!=enterprise` — will take ~30s to propagate.

infra-bot: route update accepted. Propagation to edge proxies started.

priya_oncall: started throttling job-9923 concurrency to 2 replicas. Applied k8s patch: `kubectl patch cr workload/9923 -p '{"spec":{"concurrency":2}}'`.

coco_support: customer contact (9923) acknowledged fallback; they reported degraded p95 but no complete outage. Sent status note to their SRE.

olivia_oncall: quick note on impact: ~23 customers saw increased latencies; 5 customers hit transient 503s while routing switched. We're tracking tokens and errors; will update customers as we stabilize. Prioritize SLAs.

dan_engineer: after throttling + routing: queue length dropping from 1,200 -> 420 over 12m. However autoscaler still not adding usable capacity because driver on new nodes fails. Root cause looks like driver stack regression triggered by new kernel-driver combo.

lee_infra: confirming: recent canary driver rollout (v525.70 -> v526.01) merged yesterday in infra-driver group. Nodes with older driver stable. Rolling back drivers on new nodes might help but node image bake takes ~15m per node.

priya_oncall: do we have a faster mitigation than full rollback? can we cordon affected nodes and let autoscaler choose different images? or deploy kube-level scheduling rule to prefer legacy-image nodes?

dan_engineer: created a temporary nodeSelector to prefer `gpu-image:legacy-2026-02` for new pods. `kubectl apply -f temp-sched-favor.yaml` — route change applied.

infra-bot: scheduler rule applied cluster-wide for scheduling preference to legacy image (soft preference).

priya_oncall: queue stable at ~350 and trending down. manual scale attempts still return node boot success but driver init error persists on newly provisioned nodes with new driver. Need infra follow-up: abort latest driver rollout and reimage nodes with legacy image.

lee_infra: starting emergency rollback of driver canary. Kicking off batch reimage for nodes in west-eu-gpu pool. ETA ~40m for initial 3 nodes.

olivia_oncall: handoff plan: I'm taking the next shift in 20m. Priya, document all mitigation steps and follow-ups for postmortem. Key items: driver rollback timeline, autoscaler hardening (retry/backoff), add driver healthcheck gating to autoscaler, and customer-impact log for comms.

priya_oncall: noted. filing incident ticket now and running quick impact summary:
- incident start: 4321009999
- peak queue: 1,200
- affected customers: 23 (5 with temporary 503s)
- primary cause: driver/kernal mismatch (canary driver causing Xid/OOM ripple)
- mitigations: throttled noisy tenant, route fallback to us-east, applied scheduling preference to legacy image, emergency rollback started
- open actions: driver rollout investigation, autoscaler resilience (fail fast vs. keep retrying), add pre-provision driver health check, update SLO runbook

coco_support: I've drafted a short status update for impacted customers and internal execs; will wait for final numbers before send.

olivia_oncall: handing over to me. Priya — if anything degrades after 11:45z escalate to SRE lead @lee_infra. I'll keep monitoring and make sure follow-ups are tracked.

priya_oncall: handing off to @olivia_oncall at 11:45z. All: add any notes to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 transitioned — oncall handoff recorded (from priya_oncall to olivia_oncall). Next: postmortem due in 7 days.
